source.title: LIMO: Less is More for Reasoning
source.authors: Yi-Xin Ye; Zhen Huang; Yang Xiao; Ethan Chern; Shijie Xia; Peng-Fei Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream math-benchmark performance across model sizes after applying the same fine-tuning recipe. This bears on downstream scaling, but it does not measure the original claim's held-out pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The study does not test held-out cross-entropy scaling, extrapolation of fitted loss curves, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its model-size sweep with downstream benchmark accuracy bears on V6. Other scaling-law references are cited background, not study results.
record.test_reason: Section 6.3.4 fine-tunes Qwen2.5-Instruct models of five sizes (3B to 72B) with one recipe and reports downstream math accuracy. This bears on V6 (downstream gains with scale) in a new setting: small-data reasoning SFT. It fits no scaling law and measures no pretraining loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors say AIME24 accuracy rises markedly with size (2.5 at 3B to 68.3 at 72B), while MATH500 gains are smaller. They describe the 32B–72B gap as marginal on MATH500 and smaller on AIME24, suggesting saturation and diminishing returns. Their overall conclusion concerns data efficiency (the LIMO hypothesis), not scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: Uses supervised fine-tuning on 800 LIMO examples and downstream math-benchmark accuracy across model sizes, rather than held-out pretraining loss sweeps or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured result varies with model size and benchmark: AIME24 rises markedly, while MATH500 shows little gain and a slight decrease from 32B to 72B.

fits_no_version.finding: Accuracy rises with fine-tuning dataset size (LIMO-400 to LIMO-2k), then plateaus. AIME24 goes from 57.5 to 69.6; changes between 800 and 1.2k are +0.9 and -0.2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream reasoning accuracy under SFT shows diminishing returns in fine-tuning data quantity once data is highly curated.

fits_no_version.finding: At the same 32B architecture, the pretraining data generation (Qwen1.5 vs Qwen2.5) changes post-SFT AIME24 accuracy from 9.2 to 63.3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining data quality, at fixed parameter count, strongly shifts downstream performance after SFT.

record.problems: The model-size comparison reports no uncertainty estimates. Individual values for some sizes are presented only in Figure 6 and are not given in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: None. Figure-only entries are retained for model sizes whose individual plotted values are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: No fitted quantitative relationship, no prediction of downstream accuracy from pretraining loss, no extrapolation. Model size is the only scale axis; pretraining tokens and compute are not varied.
Pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute is not measured.
No small-run fits used to predict larger runs.
No architecture-shape comparison at fixed size.
The fine-tuning dataset-size sweep reports accuracy only, with no power-law fit.

record.verdict_notes: Values for the 7B and 14B sizes, and all MATH500 values below 32B, are figure-only (Figure 6), so their rows are cannot_determine. No uncertainty is reported. AIME24 uses 4 samples per problem, so single-point differences such as 63.3 vs 68.3 are noisy. Scaling-law papers (Kaplan et al.) are cited only as background.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run loss fits or larger-run loss predictions.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep over parameters and tokens.
No architecture-shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No scaling-law tests across other modalities or training regimes.
The study tests downstream math accuracy across model sizes, but not a fitted quantitative relationship, prediction of downstream results from pretraining loss, or extrapolation to larger runs.
No analysis of loss-law fit choices, exponents, or compute-optimal allocation sensitivity.

relationships.condition: AIME24 accuracy after LIMO SFT across Qwen2.5-Instruct 3B–72B
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises monotonically in the reported points: 2.5 (3B), 63.3 (32B), 68.3 (72B) (r1, r4, r5).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased from 2.5 at 3B to 63.3 at 32B and 68.3 at 72B.

relationships.reason: There is no gain from 32B to 72B (95.6% vs 94.8%). The authors note possible saturation and diminishing returns, so improvement with scale stalls on an easy benchmark (r9, r10).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy fell from 95.6% to 94.8%, with the authors suggesting saturation and diminishing returns.
